prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK Manifesto 2024 — policy-only summary (≤500 words)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; end small-boat crossings (including ECHR exit, offshore processing, returns to France, new Department of Immigration).
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists using independent capacity and staff incentives.
- Raise the personal income tax threshold to £20,000 and lift the higher-rate threshold to £70,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping environmental levies/Net Zero targets and expanding domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Secure detention and rapid processing (offshore if needed) for illegal arrivals from safe countries; bar asylum/citizenship in such cases; no legal aid for non-citizens; deport foreign offenders after sentences.
- Restrict student dependants; close abusive courses; five-year residency/work for benefits.
- Employer Immigration Tax: raise NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt essential health/care and micro-firms).

Public spending and tax administration
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves; require 5% efficiency savings across departments; halve foreign aid; improve HMRC collections; reduce retained EU regulation.

Personal taxation and costs
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; remove VAT and environmental levies from energy bills.
- Stamp Duty: 0% below £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% above £1.5m.
- Reinstate VAT-free tourist shopping.
- Abolish inheritance tax below £2m; 20% above, with charity option.

Business and regulation
- Exempt profits up to £100k from Corporation Tax; reduce main rate to 20% (then 15% in year 3).
- Abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; introduce 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals.
- Planning fast-tracks; deregulate to ease hiring/firing; simplify the tax code.

NHS and social care
- Zero basic-rate income tax for NHS and social care staff for 3 years; expand training; write off student fees over service.
- Use independent providers domestically/overseas; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if waits exceed 3 days (GP), 3 weeks (consultant), 9 weeks (operations).
- Efficiency measures; review PFIs; “Pharmacy First” expansion; public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.
- Royal Commission on social care; curb offshore tax practices in care homes.

Energy and environment
- Scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies; fast-track North Sea and shale; expand SMR nuclear and other technologies.

Policing and justice
- Recruit 40,000 officers; expand stop and search; prioritize street policing; reduce paperwork; phase out PCSOs.
- Mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; increase justice budget; reopen magistrates’ courts; build 10,000 prison places; revise hate-crime definition.
- Reforms on grooming gangs, youth crime, and child maintenance.

Education
- Curriculum review for balance on imperialism/slavery; strengthen free speech duties.
- Schools: prohibit social transitioning/pronoun changes; parental notification; single-sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap student-loan interest; limit undergraduate numbers; expand PRUs; offer 2‑year degrees.

Brexit and constitutional
- Repeal retained EU law; abandon the Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the TCA; keep armed forces independent of EU structures.
- Leave ECHR; reform House of Lords and civil service leadership; restrict postal voting; referendum on PR; British Bill of Rights.

Housing and infrastructure
- Fast-track brownfield housing; prioritize locals/contributors for social housing.
- Reinstate mortgage-interest relief for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; strengthen leasehold protections; promote modern construction.
- Cancel remaining HS2; end ULEZ/LTNs; no ICE bans; focus on regional road/rail.
- Utilities: new model with 50% public ownership and 50% UK pension funds; cap standing charges; merge/streamline infrastructure bodies.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farm budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked schemes with direct payments; support small farms and rural economy.
- Food sourcing targets; reduce red tape; CMA powers on pricing.
- End automatic EU access; license/fee foreign vessels; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild UK processing.

Families and governance
- Transferable marriage allowance (25%) when affordable; front‑load child benefit ages 1–4; mandate single-sex public facilities; explore child‑safe smartphones; review Online Safety Act.
- Review WHO treaty participation and CBDC; replace Equality Act and DEI rules; comprehensive free‑speech bill; reform BBC (end licence fee); new national holidays; anti‑corruption unit.

Funding (party’s claims, annualised)
- Savings c. £150bn pa (efficiencies, QE interest, Net Zero/energy, benefits, aid, immigration measures) plus £10bn pa from assumed extra growth.
- Costs c. £141bn pa (tax cuts, NHS, defence, policing/justice, education, families, agriculture, fishing).
